text:
Alex: @channel Heads up — we're adjusting the release cadence starting next week. New weekly release window will be Tuesdays 10:00-14:00 PT. This tightens the freeze window to Mon 18:00 -> Tue 16:00. Rationale: reduce cross-team merge conflicts and improve oncall predictability. :loudspeaker:

Priya: Quick note: this applies to Hosted + Dedicated rollouts. Private deployments can opt out by filing a release-exemption ticket (see links below).

Jordan: If a P0 hits during the freeze, what's the hotfix path? Do we still follow the emergency deploy runbook? :thinking:

Alex: Yes — P0s follow the emergency deploy runbook. Emergency exceptions are allowed but must be approved via the release-exception process: ping @eng-releases and @oncall with rollback + monitoring plan.

Sam: Canary policy change: canaries now start 1h before the main window and are capped to 10% traffic. If canary shows regressions, auto-fallback to the previous model variant is enabled. This should reduce noisy rollouts. :gear:

Alex: Example schedule snippet for clarity:
```
Mon 18:00 - Freeze begins
Tue 09:00 - Canary starts (1h)
Tue 10:00 - Main rollout (4h window)
Tue 16:00 - Freeze ends
```

ReleaseBot: Release calendar updated: <https://calendar.redwood.ai/releases|Release Calendar> — recurring event added for the new Tuesday window.

Oncall-Bot: FYI: auto-scaling & paging thresholds remain unchanged. If latency or errors spike during the freeze, follow standard SRE incident flow and mark incidents with tag `release-freeze`.

Priya: Action items for teams: update runbooks, set canary configs to 10%, and target any non-emergency merges before Mon 18:00. Also owners: add rollback play and smoke tests to your route configs.

Jordan: Acknowledged — I'll triage outstanding patches today and coordinate with infra to validate canary gating rules.

Alex: Thanks all. We'll do a 15-min sync for rollout leads tomorrow at 16:00 PT to walk through exceptions and the new canary checklist. :calendar:
